report.source_text: After treatment, blood tests showed a decrease in LDH, beta2 micro globulin, and IgG levels, partial improvement of anaemia, with normalisation of eosinophil count (table 1). A post-treatment assessment of circulating lymphocytes by flow-cytometry showed a decrease in CD4 cells with a slight increase in CD8 cells. The B cell (CD19+, CD20+) population increased with a higher expression of kappa and lambda light chains. Globally, these findings indicated a reduction in Sézary cell count and partial improvement in B cell count and function. The patient’s skin lesions also resolved on treatment for both KS and MF and he was discharged home after a follow-up with a nurse.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 88-year-old Inuit man from Northern Quebec presented in November 2019 with a 4-month history of constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, 6 kg weight loss) preceded by rapid onset of widespread erythematous, pruritic, scaly skin lesions and violaceous subcutaneous nodules on palms and lower extremities. Physical examination revealed approximately 60 violaceous nodules on trunk and limbs, generalized scaly erythematous plaques, a small left cervical lymph node (<1 cm), and no hepatosplenomegaly. Skin biopsies confirmed two concurrent malignancies: (1) KS from violaceous nodule biopsy showing malignant vascular proliferation, spindle cells, and HHV-8 positivity by immunohistochemistry; (2) CTCL/MF from erythematous plaque biopsy showing atypical CD4-positive T-cell infiltrate with epidermotropism, partial CD7 loss, and clonal TCR gene rearrangement. HIV serology and PCR were negative, confirming HIV-negative KS status. HHV-8 PCR was positive in peripheral blood. Laboratory studies showed normocytic anemia (Hb 104 g/L), moderate eosinophilia (0.98), elevated LDH (321 U/L), and normal CD4/CD8 ratio (1.7). Imaging (MRI and PET) showed reactive lymphadenopathy without hypermetabolic skin lesions. Treatment was initiated with acitretin (10 mg daily for 4 weeks, then 30 mg daily for 8 weeks) for KS, and topical hydrocortisone cream plus UVB phototherapy for MF. Post-treatment assessment showed decreased LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, and IgG levels, partial anemia improvement, normalized eosinophil count, reduced Sézary cell count, and resolution of skin lesions for both KS and MF. Patient was discharged home with nursing follow-up.
